questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to study at a good school in a country far from home

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Had intro meetings with all the exchange students

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: In terms of getting info and practical assistance the school did a great job. However, I think the social parts of the orientation were not always great. A lot of the orientation was with freshmen which did not always work well. It can be hard to make friends with 17/18-year old freshmen who have just begun college when you are a 22-year old exchange student who is only going to be in the US for a year. I would suggest doing more social events for all the exchange students or perhaps trying to get some juniors or seniors to host some orientation events or act as buddies/tutors for the incoming exchange students.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Single, Double, Triple dorms

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Unlimited Meal plan

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is a good way to make friends and very convenient. Very expensive, but worth it in my opinion.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to preregister for courses before arriving at the school. The first week of school you could try out different courses and determine if you wanted to change some or stick with the ones you had preregistered for.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could call or email the school

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It feels stressfull in the beginning because you have to preregister before you are even at the school. During preregistration some courses might even be fully booked. However, it was my experience that in the end most courses became available and if they were not available you could email the professors and they were often times very helpful to accommodate your wishes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It greatly varies. Some courses were easier than in Copenhagen others were similar to what I would expect in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Less formal and mathematical, more about intuition. Tests and exams were spread out over the semester.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Financial Accounting, Fixed Income Securities and Derivatives, Financial Modelling, Public Finance, Intro to Game Theory and Strategic Thinking, Behavioral Economics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Behavioral Economics, Intro to Game Theory and Strategic Thinking

Both courses had great professors and were very interesting.

Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Anything you liked there was a club for it. From football to quidditch to political debates.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I joined a football/soccer team which I enjoyed a lot. Great community and a great way to meet locals at the university.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Lots of good hikes in the finger lakes area. See Niagara Falls. Go to NYC.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It took some time, but relatively easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a club (academic or non-academic), in my experience that was definitely the best way to meet locals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Took some time to adjust to campus life.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Everyone is very open and friendly. It is not weird to start a conversation with a complete stranger - even halfway through the semester.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Join a club
2. Live on campus (preferably west campus)
3. Explore campus, don't just stay in the buildings where you have classes. Campus is so big and they have a cinema, bowling alleys, a gaming room and lots of other stuff. Even if you keep exploring for your full exchange you feel like you haven't seen everything

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Best ways to get to campus:

Fly to ithaca (expensive)
Fly to syracuse and take uber from there (approx 1hr.) (less expensive)
Bus from NYC to Ithaca (ourbus or flixbus provide good service) (cheapest option)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making new friends and exploring a new country/culture

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being far away from home and trying to build a new daily life in a new country.
